react.buildToolingNote: JSX cannot run in Node directly; esbuild bundle step required before tests/render (see reactBuildToolingOneTime).
react.harnessFixNote: R-1: React SSR inserts <!-- --> text-separator comments ("$<!-- -->49"); the shared price assertion needed a documented normalization in the React test. R-5: esbuild ESM bundling of CJS react-dom/server failed with "Dynamic require of util is not supported" once renderToString moved into the bundled entry; fixed by externalizing react/react-dom in react/build.mjs.

basenative.implementationNote: Final implementation is the declarative template + hydrate() path (v2). The v1 direct-DOM-binding version (69 lines / 2186 bytes / ~547 tokens) is preserved in RUN_LOG.md.
basenative.appFixNote: BN-1 (in v1): diamond subscription — an effect reading both a signal and a computed derived from it ran twice per change; the fix (subscribe to the computed, read the source with .peek()) is carried into v2, which then passed on its first run.

react.buildToolingNote: JSX + react-dom/client bundled by esbuild before the jsdom test could import it.
react.harnessFixNote: R-2: Node 24 getter-only global navigator broke jsdom global setup. R-3: React 19 mount effect + setState settle asynchronously — test needed an act()+macrotask settle before asserting; BaseNative effects are synchronous and needed none.

reactBuildToolingOneTime.note: One-time hand-written build script React needed in this repo; BaseNative needed no equivalent. Counted once in the amortization, not per task.

agentDocsBundle.note: One-time LLM context cost for BaseNative. React needs no equivalent (its API is in model weights).

amortization.explanation: No break-even exists at this task size: the average per-task code-token saving is -16 (negative — BaseNative code was slightly LARGER than React code on these two small tasks), so the one-time docs cost of 2364 net tokens is never recovered through per-task code-size savings. The docs bundle pays off through avoided syntax errors and zero build/tooling friction (see BENCHMARK.md), not through smaller code. Larger, template-heavy tasks may change the per-task sign; these two tasks do not show it.
